Subject: DPA sequencing & TIA clarifications for EU/UK pilot

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to test Redwood for a small EU/UK clinical analytics pilot. Legal has one gating concern before we start: how you expect us to handle international transfer coverage for the pilot data. Specifically: 

- Will Redwood provide SCCs + an EU TIA, or is the expectation that we sign a UK Addendum/IDTA in parallel?
- We have a short procurement window: can you deliver the subprocessor snapshot and logging evidence within 10 business days?
- Do you support routing guarantees (EU-only processing) for this pilot, or do we need an on-prem arrangement?

I attached our completed TIA questionnaire to make the asks concrete (Pharmaco_TIA_Questionnaire.xlsx). Jurgen (cc) will handle the legal checklist — he asked whether Redwood will accept limited redlines to the UK Addendum and whether a bespoke TIA is possible for regulated datasets.

Can you confirm your proposed sequencing (SCCs -> TIA -> UK addendum) and an ETA for the evidence pack? We prefer to avoid a bespoke contract if signatures on standard SCC+Addendum suffice, but we need clarity on evidence turnaround and routing controls first.

Best,
Sara Varela
Head of Data Governance
Pharmaco Therapeutics

Attachment: Pharmaco_TIA_Questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.example

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 26 Sep 2028 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA sequencing & TIA clarifications for EU/UK pilot

Sara — really appreciate the clear asks and the completed questionnaire. Short answers up front:

1) Sequencing: we propose the following minimum path for the pilot: SCCs (standard EU Commission clauses) executed first -> provide subprocessor snapshot + evidence -> scope a targeted TIA (technical and organizational safeguards mailbox) for the pilot dataset -> execute UK Addendum/IDTA if data residency or UK subjects are in scope.

2) Evidence ETA: we can deliver a compressed evidence pack (subprocessor snapshot, logging retention summary, TLS key custody statements) in 7 business days. A fuller audit packet (SOC2 excerpts, HSM attestations) is ~3 weeks.

3) Routing: for the short pilot we can provide region routing guarantees (EU-only) via config at ingestion and ensure no fallback to non-EU endpoints. That is not the same as on‑prem, but we will include a routing SLA clause for the pilot. If you require physical on-prem, that’s a separate engagement.

We can accept limited redlines to the UK Addendum focused on incident notification and Subprocessor onboarding notice periods; we typically cannot accept unilateral indemnity expansions. If Pharmaco wants a bespoke TIA, we can discuss — our default is to scope the TIA narrowly for the pilot (data categories, retention, pseudonymization measures, access controls), which usually satisfies regulated customers without a full bespoke agreement.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to deliver compressed evidence pack (7 business days) — we will attach Redwood_Subprocessor_Snapshot.pdf.
- Legal sync: loop in Marissa to prepare redlines for the UK Addendum and confirm which redlines are acceptable.
- Technical call to lock routing config the week of Oct 2.

I’m copying Kim (security) and Laura (privacy ops) so they see the timeline.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessor_Snapshot.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

Team — forwarding Pharmaco thread. Key asks are: 7-business-day compressed evidence pack, EU-only routing for the pilot, and limited redlines to the UK Addendum around notification windows. I called out the parts I think we can agree to and what needs legal sign-off below. Please review and advise on redlines/turnaround.

My suggested positions: 
- Evidence pack: agree to compressed pack in 7 business days (subprocessor list + logging retention + KMS outline).
- Routing: agree to config-based EU-only routing with SLA clause; add fallback protection preventing automatic reroute to non-EU regions unless explicitly authorized.
- UK Addendum: accept redlines limited to notification periods, contact points, and a 30-day remediation window for subprocessor issues. Reject any attempt to add open-ended broad indemnity.

Marissa — can you draft Redwood_UK_Addendum_Redlines_v1.docx capturing the above? If we can get a DR/ops acceptance on routing language and a yes on evidence ETA, I will propose the Oct 3 technical call to Pharmaco.

Sara / Jurgen — thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. Attached are Redwood's initial redlines for the UK Addendum and a short summary of the compressed evidence pack we will deliver next week. High level:

- We have drafted limited redlines that accept a 30-day remediation window for subprocessor issues, a 72-hour incident notification for critical incidents, and a 10 business day notice for subprocessor changes during the pilot. We do not accept requests to expand indemnity beyond the standard DPA.
- Compressed evidence pack will include: current subprocessor roster, retention & logging summary, TLS/HSM custody statement, and screenshots of routing config (ETA: 7 business days).
- We will provide a DocuSign-ready Addendum if Pharmaco confirms acceptance of these redlines.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether Pharmaco wants the DocuSign flow or a redline exchange via email.
2) Technical call to confirm routing + ingestion config on Oct 3 or Oct 4 (we have an opening Oct 3 at 10:00 AM CET).
3) Redwood to deliver compressed evidence pack by Oct 5.

If that works, I will put the DocuSign envelope together and share a link.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference
